explanation: Mali's wealth came from gold fields and trade across the Sahara. A Catalan map of 1375 shows him enthroned, holding up a piece of gold.

claims.text: Mansa Musa, ruler of the Mali Empire, passed through Cairo on his pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324.
According to the chronicler al-Umari, Mansa Musa spent and gave away so much gold in Cairo that its value there fell.
Sundiata Keita founded Mali long before 1324, and Askia Muhammad and Sunni Ali ruled the later Songhai Empire.
The Mali Empire's wealth came from gold and trade across the Sahara.
The Catalan Atlas of 1375 shows Mansa Musa enthroned and holding up a piece of gold.
